verdict_reason: Re-measured this round and the fix is correct on every point I raised. (a) The hook substitution is provably lossless: ln_f(layers[-1] output) reproduces HF hidden_states[-1] to max|diff| = 0.000e+00 on gpt2, distilgpt2 and pythia-160m, so the scored set is exactly blocks 0..L-1 with no LayerNorm entry and no missing block. (b) HEAD-TO-HEAD against the official andyrdt/refusal_direction kernel, which I fetched and ported verbatim (forward PRE-hooks on every block, positions=[-1], fp64 accumulator): BLME's per-layer full_direction at slot l equals the official mean_diff at resid_pre[l+1] with max relative error 7.4e-06 (gpt2) / 9.7e-05 (pythia-160m) and cosine 1.0000000000 -- the residual is float32-vs-float64 accumulation, nothing else. (c) auc_at_depth_100 is restored: gpt2 0.8125, distilgpt2 0.9167, pythia-160m 0.5417, none NaN. (d) best_layer_fraction now spans the full range (gpt2 1.0000, distilgpt2 1.0000, pythia-160m 0.0000). (e) best_layer_separability_auc is 0.8125 on gpt2, which my independent per-block sweep confirms is the model's true maximum ([0.625, 0.604, 0.646, 0.625, 0.646, 0.688, 0.729, 0.708, 0.708, 0.750, 0.771, 0.8125]). I also REFUTE my own prior objection about the dropped embedding: hidden_states[0] scores 0.4792 (gpt2), 0.4792 (distilgpt2) and 0.3750 (pythia-160m) -- at or below chance on all three, never the argmax, and on pythia-160m its difference-of-means is exactly zero in some CV folds. The 0.6458 I previously attributed to 'layer 0 = the embedding' on pythia-160m is block-0's OUTPUT, which IS scored and IS the argmax (best_layer 0). Remaining items are CONFIG or latent, listed below. Test status: tests/tasks/parity/test_repe_refusal_direction_parity.py and test_comprehensive_parity.py::test_repe_refusal_direction both pass (99 passed across the repe unit + parity files).
comparable_reason: Re-measured over the 51 archived models for which I could resolve a HF config. direction_norm is a raw scale readout and not comparable: Spearman +0.790 with vocab_size (p = 5.7e-12), +0.571 with log(params), +0.494 with d_model, +0.385 with n_layers. best_layer is an absolute index (+0.610 with n_layers, p = 2e-06) and best_layer_separability_auc carries +0.535 with vocab and +0.481 with n_layers. The two AUC-style columns are dimensionless and the depth-normalised index is nearly architecture-free (see normalized_ok), so the metric family is comparable in principle -- but at the shipped 12 vs 12 prompts with cv_splits = 3 the sampling noise swamps the between-model spread: sweeping the CV seed 0..29 gives 0.7319 +/- 0.1007 (gpt2, range [0.3958, 0.8542]), 0.4556 +/- 0.1471 (pythia-160m, [0.1042, 0.7500]) and 0.8500 +/- 0.0898 (distilgpt2, [0.6250, 0.9792]). Shipped seed 42 lands +0.80 / +0.59 / +0.74 sd above each model's own seed mean. A three-model gap of 0.54 -> 0.92 is only ~2.5 seed-sd wide, and no interval is emitted.
normalized_variant: best_layer_scalenorm (= best_layer / n_layers; NORMALIZERS in src/blme/normalization.py). The task separately emits the in-task best_layer_fraction (= best_layer / largest scored layer index), which is the same quantity with the correct denominator.
normalized_ok_reason: It works. In the archive best_layer carries rho +0.610 with n_layers (p = 2e-06) while best_layer_fraction carries -0.161 (p = 0.26), -0.274 with d_model (p = 0.052) and -0.310 with vocab -- the depth readout is removed, not merely rescaled. Post-fix it also uses the full [0, 1] range (pythia-160m 0.0000, gpt2 and distilgpt2 1.0000), which the pre-fix denominator could not reach.
github_reason: Fetched pipeline/submodules/generate_directions.py from the official repo this round and RAN its kernel head-to-head. get_mean_activations installs a forward PRE-hook per block that accumulates (1/n) * input[0][:, positions, :] into a float64 cache; get_mean_diff returns harmful-mean minus harmless-mean. I ported that verbatim (batch_size 1, positions=[-1], fp64) and ran it on the same bundled 12 + 12 prompts as BLME. BLME slot l == official resid_pre[l+1] to max rel-err 7.4e-06 / 9.7e-05 with cos 1.0000000000 on gpt2 / pythia-160m. Protocol still differs and I did not run their full pipeline: they take positions = range(-len(eoi_toks), 0) over chat-template post-instruction tokens (BLME: the single last token of an untemplated prompt), n_train = 128 + 128 pre-filtered by baseline refusal score (BLME: the bundled 12 + 12), their candidate set is resid_pre[0..L-1] and select_direction additionally prunes the deepest 20% (BLME scores blocks 0..L-1, i.e. it drops resid_pre[0] and adds resid_post[L-1]), and they select by minimum bypass_score subject to induce_score > 0 and kl_score < 0.1 rather than by argmax held-out AUC.
paper_reason: Arditi et al. publish no direction-intrinsic quantity this task could reproduce. Every number in the paper is intervention-dependent -- refusal / safety scores after directional ablation or activation addition, and the Table 5 triples (Llama-3 8B: layer 12/32, position -5, bypass -9.715, induce 7.681, KL 0.064) -- all of which require the ablation and addition hooks BLME does not implement. There is no published norm, cosine or AUROC of the difference-of-means vector itself; the cosine-similarity results appear only as unlabelled heat maps (Figs. 5, 24). The repo's committed run artifacts are a re-run, not the paper's run (Llama-3 8B repo -9.855 / 7.676 / 0.0588 vs paper -9.715 / 7.681 / 0.064), so they are not a substitute anchor either.
confounds_reason: direction_norm rho +0.790 with vocab_size (p = 5.7e-12) and +0.571 with log(params) over 51 archived models -- it is a magnitude in un-normalised residual-stream units and tracks scale directly. best_layer rho +0.610 with n_layers. The AUC columns are much cleaner (separability_auc rho +0.057 with d_model, p = 0.69; +0.399 with vocab, p = 0.0037) and best_layer_fraction is architecture-free. Separately, and more important for the paper's framing: the construct is not refusal. gpt2 and distilgpt2 are base models with no refusal behaviour whatsoever and score 0.8125 and 0.9167 -- the bundled harmful/harmless split is separable as a TOPIC (weapons/hacking/drugs vs cooking/gardening/email), so a high value here is evidence of topical linear structure, not of a refusal mechanism. The class docstring says this; the task name does not.
defects: CONFIG: the estimate is dominated by sampling noise and the task emits no interval. 12 harmful vs 12 harmless with cv_splits = 3 makes each fold a 4-vs-4 AUC, quantised to 1/16. Sweeping the CV seed 0..29 at the headline layer: gpt2 0.7319 +/- 0.1007 (range [0.3958, 0.8542]), pythia-160m 0.4556 +/- 0.1471 ([0.1042, 0.7500]), distilgpt2 0.8500 +/- 0.0898 ([0.6250, 0.9792]). The shipped seed 42 sits +0.80 / +0.59 / +0.74 sd above each model's own mean, so the headline is optimistic by roughly 0.07-0.09 AUC purely from the seed. Fix is CONFIG-side (more prompts) plus a new interval output; the estimator itself is correct.

CODE (latent, not triggered on any model I ran): the depth axis is normalised by the largest layer index with a FINITE AUC (`layer_idxs.max()` over `ordered`), while best_layer_fraction is normalised by the largest index in per_layer (`_scored_idx[-1]`). If a deep layer yields NaN AUC (e.g. non-finite activations under fp16) the two denominators diverge and auc_at_depth_100 silently becomes 'the deepest layer that happened to produce a number' rather than depth 1.0. The code comment two lines above warns against exactly this rescaling at the shallow end, then does it at the deep end.

The deepest scored position is block L-1's OUTPUT, which is one step past the official candidate set (resid_pre[0..L-1]) and inside the deepest 20% that select_direction prunes. It is a legitimate residual-stream position and it is the argmax on gpt2 (0.8125) and distilgpt2 (0.9167), so the choice is defensible -- but it should be documented as a deliberate departure rather than inherited from the HF hidden_states layout.

separability_auc and mean_projection_gap can disagree in sign at the same layer (pythia-160m: AUC 0.5417 > 0.5 but gap -13.83, because AUC is rank-based and the gap is a mean). Not a bug, but the two headline numbers can tell opposite stories.

CODE (cosmetic): `_rd_hooked` is written in both branches of `collect` and never read; the task emits no flag telling a consumer whether the deepest entry is the hooked block output or the trimmed fallback.
fix: Nothing required for correctness. Optional hardening: (1) normalise BOTH depth axes by the same denominator and emit the denominator (or a `depth_axis_max_layer` field) so a consumer can tell when depth 1.0 is not the model's last block; (2) raise the bundled prompt set well above 12 + 12 and/or emit a bootstrap/seed-resampled interval on separability_auc -- at the shipped n the seed-to-seed sd (0.09-0.15) is comparable to the whole cross-model spread; (3) drop or emit the unused `_rd_hooked` flag; (4) note in the docstring that the deepest scored layer is resid_post[L-1], one position past Arditi's candidate set. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): the registered twin best_layer/n_layers is RED and should be removed -- it is a near-duplicate of the in-task best_layer_fraction (archive Pearson +0.9991, Spearman +0.9905) built on the WRONG denominator, which is exactly the defect item (1) above describes. Because the deepest scored index is n_layers-1, the twin's attainable ceiling is (L-1)/L -- 0.833 at L = 6 against 0.979 at L = 48 -- so every model whose peak sits at the last block reports a pure monotone function of depth. After the R14 hook fix that is the common case: 11 of 20 freshly run models saturate at the deepest block, and there the twin fails to remove the depth term -- raw rho(n_layers) = +0.892 (p = 1e-07) -> +0.505 (p = 0.02) for best_layer_scalenorm, against -0.032 (p = 0.9) for best_layer_fraction on the same 20 models. On the 66-model archive it also manufactures a vocabulary association, rho(vocab) -0.042 (p = 0.74) -> -0.322 (p = 0.008), since n_layers itself carries +0.395 with vocab. Delete the NORMALIZERS entry and keep best_layer_fraction.
